title: Harness definition
description: The normative description of `.agents/harnesses/<id>/harness.yaml` (ADR 0015 §2). Structural validation only: checks that depend on the filesystem, on compiling a CEL expression, or on agreement between separate parts of the document are enforced by the loader after this schema passes.

spec_version.description: Version of this format the document is written against. Advisory: the loader validates the token and does not otherwise branch on it. Parsing is additive across versions, so no document is read differently by version; the behavior of a declared construct may still be corrected uniformly across all of them (ADR 0015 §4, partially superseded by ADR 0019 §6).

id.description: Harness identifier. Must equal the containing directory name.

description.description: Human-facing summary. Documentation only — the loader does not read it.

roles.description: Roles by identifier. At least one is required. Identifiers become path segments in run scratchpads, so they are constrained like every other id in this format.

execution.description: How roles are scheduled. Absent means the runtime's default scheduling.

hooks.description: Hook handlers by lifecycle event. Note that only `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call` and `role_stop` currently reach an adapter; handlers on the other events are accepted here and never run.

context.description: Context collected once, before any role runs.

output.description: Schemas that role outcomes are validated against.

schemas.description: Outcome schemas by kind. `builtin:finding` is bound to the `finding` kind here rather than described as generally available, because the loader rejects it under any other kind.

filtering.description: Finding classification strategies. Named `filtering` because in spec 0.1 through 0.3 these removed findings; as of 0.4 none of them does, and the key is kept rather than renamed so older documents load unchanged (ADR 0019 §3, §6).

findings.description: Applied in order. `builtin:actionable` marks any finding that is not `validation.status: verified` with at least one `validation.evidence` item as unsubstantiated: still published, but excluded from run status and from the triage queue.

policy.description: Default policy identifier, resolved against `.agents/policies/<id>.yaml`. A role may override it.

default_allowed_commands.description: Commands allowed to every role that does not state its own list.

nonBlankString.description: A string with at least one non-whitespace character. Distinct from nonEmptyString because the loader trims these particular lists before checking them, so " " is empty as far as it is concerned.

idToken.description: Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit; never a path separator or '..', because these become path segments.

role.description: One role. Either declared inline, or pulled from a shared role file with `ref` and optionally overridden.

ref.description: Identifier of a shared role at `.agents/agents/<id>/agent.md`. Sibling keys here override that file's frontmatter.

description.description: What the role does. Required unless supplied by a referenced role file.

enabled.description: CEL expression deciding whether the role runs. Absent means always enabled. Compiled at load.

prompt_path.description: Prompt file, absolute or relative to the harness directory. Mutually exclusive with `prompt`.

timeout_ms.description: Role timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 600000.

allowed_commands.description: Commands this role may run, overriding `default_allowed_commands`.

required_capabilities.description: Adapter capabilities the role needs. Defaults to none.

policy.description: Policy identifier for this role, overriding the harness default.

execution.description: Which keys apply depends on `mode`. Keys belonging to another mode are ignored by the loader rather than rejected, so they are permitted here — the schema describes the format as implemented.

mode.description: parallel: all enabled roles run concurrently. chain: roles run in sequence and the first failure stops the chain. validation-loop: implementation roles alternate with validation roles until validation passes or the round cap is reached.

order.description: chain only. Step order; every entry must name a declared role.

pass_check.description: chain only. Command run in the workspace after all roles complete; exit 0 means the run passed. The authoritative success gate.

max_rounds.description: validation-loop only. Maximum rounds; defaults to 1.

hookCommand.description: Command to run. `$HARNESS_DIR` expands to the harness directory.

hookMatcher.description: Regular expression over tool names; absent matches all.

excludedHandlerType.description: Handlers are commands only. `prompt:` and `http:` handler types are deliberately out of spec, and are declared here so that using one is reported as an unsupported handler type rather than as a misspelling.

toolCallHandlers.description: Handlers for a tool-call event. These are the events that reach an adapter.

applies_to.description: Event classes this handler registers on; absent means all of them. Valid only on tool-call events.
Never valid here — event-class scoping applies only to tool-call events. Declared so that using it is reported as a misplaced key rather than an unknown one, which lets the loader explain why.

contextProvider.description: One context provider. Keys other than `use` are provider parameters and are deliberately unconstrained here; the provider registry validates them.

recordOutputSchema.title: record
recordOutputSchema.description: Required fields for an outcome of this kind.

required.description: Fields that must be present on the outcome.

data_required.description: Fields that must be present on the outcome's data object.

outputSchema.description: The `finding` kind only: either the builtin schema or an explicit record of required fields.
